title: Building a Multi-Agent Coding Harness from Scratch and Why It Failed: Inside m9g-agent-corps vs. OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Antigravity
ledeHtml: We built m9g-agent-corps, a 28-module Python coding harness in src/ag_harness/ with 169 passing unit tests. On daily multi-file tasks, it lost on speed and reliability to Oh-My-OpenAgent, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Google Antigravity. Six inner-loop flaws caused that failure, including unwired edit hooks, regex status parsing, and 300-second buffered subprocesses. We retired the outer loop and extracted seven stateless tools into m9g-mcp.
hubTitle: Why Our 28-Module Coding Harness Failed Against OmO, OpenCode & Claude Code (and Extracting m9g-mcp)
hubDesc: Post-mortem of 6 architectural failure modes in a from-scratch 28-module harness and how we extracted 7 deterministic verification tools into m9g-mcp.
bodyHtml:
TL;DR: Post-Mortem Summary and Architecture Pivot
  • 28 modules and 169 passing unit tests in src/ag_harness/. We built and unit-tested six core subsystems: ImmutablePrefixBuilder for 95% Gemini implicit cache hits ($0.10/1M vs. $2.00/1M), HashlineEditor (4-char SHA-256 line hashes, ±25-line drift relocation, under 1 ms AST compile checks) plus skeletonize_python_code() (75% to 90% AST token compression), shadow GIT_INDEX_FILE checkpoints (WorkspaceCheckpointManager) with SQLite WAL turn logs (SessionStore), FiveTierHookPipeline with IntentGate and GitMemoryFaultSidecar, topological wave execution (DAGEngine, TodoManager, BoulderEngine, and c1..c8 component checks), and a Windows-to-WSL2 bridge with a GF(2^8) terminal QR remote PWA.
  • Six inner-loop kernel flaws broke daily reliability. Passing unit tests in isolation did not save the live loop. argon_omo_substrate.py sat unwired from main.py and agy_workers.py; WorkerHandoffReport.parse_from_markdown() defaulted truncated worker turns to SUCCESS; spawn_agy_worker() locked CLI subagents inside 300-second buffered subprocess.run black boxes; Rule-1 mandatory delegation and 19 bound tools added a 78 s to 142 s relay tax on 1-to-3 file edits; cap_tool_output() deleted lines 120 to 380 via middle-out slicing; and StreamLoopMonitor hard-killed workers on three repeated calls.
  • Extracting seven stateless tools into m9g-mcp worked. Instead of maintaining a second outer loop against OmO's persistent Bun and Python eval kernels, OpenCode's Go/TS event bus and LSP loop, Claude Code's single-process exact-edit loop, and Antigravity's container runtime, we packaged our seven stateless tools into a JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio MCP server (m9g-power-tools) that runs inside those harnesses.
Engineered Scope
28 Modules
src/ag_harness/ (~640 KB, 169 unit tests)
Subsystems Built
8 Components
Hashline, AST Skel, Shadow Git, WAL, DAG
Root Failure Modes
6 Kernel Flaws
Unwired hooks, regex handoff, blocking CLI
Architectural Pivot
7 MCP Tools
m9g-mcp stdio server for OmO/Claude/OpenCode
TL;DR Video Walkthrough: 40s Architectural Post-Mortem (gemini-omni-1.1-flash) Direct MP4 Stream (blog2-wrapup-omni.mp4) ↗

Why we tried to build a standalone multi-agent coding harness

During a 1-billion-token weekend engineering sprint on gemini-4-carbon and gemini-3.8-flash, three failure modes kept recurring in standard LLM coding sessions. Reading full source files into the frontier prompt bloated context windows. Line-number drift across sequential edits corrupted files. Failed edits polluted the user's staged .git/index and forced manual cleanup.

We bet that a custom three-tier harness named m9g-agent-corps (CLI aliases m9g-code and m9g) could fix all three problems at once. In our design, a Tier-1 Higher Brain (APEX: gemini-4-carbon and gemini-2.5-pro) held cross-file architecture in cached memory while dispatching file-level edits to isolated Tier-2 (MIDDLE: gemini-2.5-pro-preview) and Tier-3 (WORKHORSE/SCOUT: gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-3.5-flash-lite) workers. Across several weeks, we wrote 28 Python modules (~640 KB) in src/ag_harness/ and 17 test suites with 169 passing unit and integration tests.

Figure 1 (M9G-TR-2026-02). Architecture of m9g-agent-corps (src/ag_harness/). Left: Tier 1 orchestrator (gemini-4-carbon / APEX) with immutable prefix caching, two-tier skill loading, and AST skeletonization. Center: Tier 2 (MIDDLE) and Tier 3 (WORKHORSE / SCOUT) workers. Right: the six inner-loop flaws that caused the standalone harness to trail OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Antigravity.

What we built across 28 modules and 169 passing unit tests

D:\git\m9g-agent-corps was not a thin prompt wrapper. We built concrete implementations for all eight components codified in HARNESS2_8_COMPONENTS (argon_omo_substrate.py:617: c1: system_prompt, c2: context_policy, c3: long_term_memory, c4: tool_guidance, c5: sub_agents, c6: skills_and_guardrails, c7: scripts, c8: hooks_and_plugins):

Investigation 01 • Token & Cache Economics

Immutable Prefix Caching & Tail-Only Dynamic Injection

ImmutablePrefixBuilder (argon_omo_substrate.py:766) and corps.jsonc preserve Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 4 Carbon's 95% implicit cache discount ($0.10/1M cached vs. $2.00/1M uncached). The builder strips dynamic timestamps (Generated:, Timestamp:, Current git status:) from message index 0, locks <immutable_system_prompt>, <immutable_agents_md>, sorted <immutable_tool_schemas>, and <immutable_repo_map> under a verified SHA-256 prefix_hash, caps static prefix text at 28,000 characters, and appends turn-varying state (<memory_sidecar_constraints>, <intent_gate_status>) only at the user message tail.

Investigation 02 • Drift-Tolerant Code Mutation

SHA-256 Hashline Editing & AST Skeletonization

In hashline_tools.py (508 lines), HashlineEditor.hashline_read() prefixes every line with a 4-character SHA-256 content hash (L{n}:{hash}|) and loads parent-directory AGENTS.md files once per session via _SURFACED_DIR_AGENTS. hashline_edit() relocates drifted spans inside a ±25-line window (_locate_matching_span), applies hunks bottom-up (reverse=True) so line indices never shift mid-batch, and runs Python compile() AST validation in under 1 ms. In context_controller.py, skeletonize_python_code() reduces Python files to signatures and docstrings, cutting token count by 75% to 90%.

Investigation 03 • Atomic Workspace State

Shadow GIT_INDEX_FILE Checkpoints & SQLite WAL Store

In checkpoint.py (685 lines), WorkspaceCheckpointManager._capture_git_tree_sha() snapshots dirty worktrees and untracked files without touching the user's staged .git/index. It copies .git/index into a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, sets GIT_INDEX_FILE, runs git add -A and git write-tree to record a 40-character tree SHA, and restores state via git read-tree plus git checkout-index -a -f with a 250-file Copy-on-Write fallback. In session_store.py (1,508 lines), a thread-locked SQLite WAL state machine logs turn transitions from CREATED through STREAMING and TOOL_PENDING to COMMITTED or ROLLED_BACK.

Investigation 04 • Self-Healing & Continual Memory

5-Tier Hook Pipeline, IntentGate & Git Fault Sidecar

In argon_omo_substrate.py, FiveTierHookPipeline coordinates five stages: Tier 1 loads past fault rules from GitMemoryFaultSidecar (an isolated Git repo at .m9g/fault_memory); Tier 2 (IntentGate) classifies prompts into information, judgment, plan, or build and blocks mutating tools until prove_plan() runs; Tier 3 runs repair_json_arguments() on malformed tool JSON and verifies hashline spans; Tier 4 trims tracebacks via extract_concise_stack_trace(); and Tier 5 commits resolved faults as YAML-frontmatter lessons (cue, lesson, evidence).

Investigation 05 • Multi-Wave Orchestration

11-Agent Roster, 16 Categories, DAGEngine & Boulder

Modeled after OmO's specialist roles, gemini_roster.py (649 lines) defines 11 agents (sisyphus, oracle, metis, momus, hephaestus, flash-worker, qa-executor, explore, librarian, code-reviewer, gate-reviewer) across 16 task categories. ulw_engine.py pairs TodoManager with persistent BoulderEngine continuation state, and dag_engine.py (450 lines) runs Kahn's topological wave sort with CyclicDependencyError detection, bounded semaphore concurrency, and upstream handoff injection.

Investigation 06 • Cross-OS & Mobile Control

WSL2 Bridge, GF(2⁸) Terminal QR PWA & System Doctor

In wsl_bridge.py (442 lines), WSLPathTranslator converts Windows and WSL2 paths in both directions, forwards credentials via WSLENV, and reaps POSIX process groups cleanly. In remote_control.py (849 lines), pure-Python Galois Field GF(2^8) Reed-Solomon QR encoding renders pairing codes in Unicode half-blocks (▀▄█) for mobile control, paired with herdr_bridge.py IPC reporting and run_system_doctor() in doctor.py.

Six kernel mistakes that broke our standalone harness in daily work

All 169 unit tests across 17 test files passed. Yet on real multi-file refactors and bug fixes, m9g-agent-corps ran slower and broke more often than OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Antigravity. Auditing our own call graph exposed a hard systems truth: unit-tested helper modules do not make a reliable coding harness when the inner execution loop is loosely coupled. Six specific kernel mistakes caused the failure:

Failure Cause 1: Leaving argon_omo_substrate.py unwired from main.py and agy_workers.py

We implemented FiveTierHookPipeline, IntentGate, HashlineEditor, ImmutablePrefixBuilder, and TmuxSubscriptionWatcher inside argon_omo_substrate.py (1,245 lines) and tested them in run_argon_smoke_benchmarks(). Yet the live REPL loop (stream_turn() in main.py:124) and worker launcher (spawn_agy_worker() in agy_workers.py:427) instantiated google.antigravity.Agent(config=config) directly. Its built-in runtime tools (edit_file, replace_file_content, run_command) bypassed FiveTierHookPipeline, IntentGate, and HashlineEditor on every call. Our prompts asked workers in English prose to check their edits, whereas OmO, OpenCode, and Claude Code enforce edit validation, permission checks, and diagnostics inside the single mandatory tool-dispatch function.

Failure Cause 2: Regex status parser defaulting truncated turns to SUCCESS (agy_workers.py:296-305)

When the Tier-1 Higher Brain delegated work to a Tier-2 or Tier-3 subagent, WorkerHandoffReport.parse_from_markdown() never received a typed execution result. Instead, it asked the worker to print a Markdown footer and scraped that text with a regular expression:

Source Post-Mortem: src/ag_harness/agy_workers.py (Lines 296 to 305) Ref: M9G-TR-2026-02
status_match = re.search(r"#{1,4}\s*STATUS:\s*([A-Za-z_]+)", raw_text, re.IGNORECASE)
if status_match: status = status_match.group(1).upper()
elif not raw_text.strip() or raw_text.lstrip().startswith(("[Worker Execution Error", "Traceback")): status = "FAILED"
else: status = "SUCCESS"

How this corrupted multi-wave DAGs: Whenever a worker hit its output token limit, truncated mid-sentence, exited a CLI subprocess with a non-zero return code (check=False at line 415), or answered without a ## STATUS: heading, parse_from_markdown() returned status = "SUCCESS" with files_modified=[]. DAGEngine marked the failed wave complete and scheduled downstream waves onto an unedited worktree.

Failure Cause 3: 300-second buffered subprocess.run black boxes (agy_workers.py:409-424)

To invoke external CLI workers (agy.exe -p or omo.exe -p), spawn_agy_worker() called a blocking subprocess.run inside asyncio.to_thread:

Source Post-Mortem: src/ag_harness/agy_workers.py (Lines 409 to 417) Ref: M9G-TR-2026-02
proc = await asyncio.to_thread(
  subprocess.run, cmd, cwd=abs_ws, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, check=False
)

Why buffered subprocesses lose to live kernels: Setting capture_output=True hid all stdout and stderr for up to five minutes. The orchestrator could not tail live progress (unlike OmO's task_output(mode="tail") or monitor), could not steer a drifting worker mid-turn (unlike OmO's task_send or bash_input), and threw away every intermediate diagnostic if subprocess.TimeoutExpired fired at 300 seconds.

Failure Cause 4: Rule-1 mandatory delegation tax and 19-tool prompt bloat (config.py:381-485)

In config.py:457, Rule 1 forbade the Higher Brain from reading 500-line files directly and forced it to call spawn_agy_worker() for every multi-file edit, UI build, reverse-engineering pass, or test run. At the same time, _resolve_agent_tools() bound 19 Higher-Brain tools and up to 28,000 characters of static prompt prefix on Turn 1.

Why this tripled latency on 1-to-3 file edits: On a three-file bug fix, Claude Code, OpenCode, and OmO read the target spans, apply exact edits, and run diagnostics inside one process in 24 to 34 seconds. Rule 1 forced a cold-start relay: the Higher Brain spawned a fresh worker process, the worker re-read files from disk and compressed its findings into a 300-word Markdown summary, and the Higher Brain tried to debug failing tests after that summary had stripped the exact cross-file type signatures it needed.

Failure Cause 5: Destructive middle-out string slicing (hooks.py:23-25 and subagents.py:34)

To cap token-per-minute burn, cap_tool_output() truncated any tool output longer than 12,000 characters by keeping the first 4,000 characters and the last 8,000 characters, while trim_context_for_tier2() cut the center out of file_context:

Source Post-Mortem: src/ag_harness/hooks.py (Lines 23 to 25) & subagents.py (Lines 35 to 40) Ref: M9G-TR-2026-02
DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CHARS = 12000  |  HEAD_CHARS = 4000, TAIL_CHARS = 8000
file_context[:keep_chars // 2] + "\n...[TRIMMED]...\n" + file_context[-(keep_chars // 2):]

Why middle-out slicing triggers hallucinated code: In a 600-line Python module or a multi-failure pytest log, cap_tool_output() deletes lines 120 to 380 right out of the middle. Blind to those deleted definitions, workers invented function bodies or looped on repeated file reads. OmO, OpenCode, and Claude Code never delete the middle of a file read; they paginate with explicit line offset and limit parameters so the model always sees contiguous line numbers.

Failure Cause 6: Hard-kill loop breaking and nested orchestrator overhead (agy_workers.py:557)

When StreamLoopMonitor saw three identical tool calls, _run_worker() executed break on the response stream and aborted the worker with STATUS: FAILED, discarding its entire working context. Worse, when m9g-agent-corps spawned agy or omo as a CLI worker without disabling inner delegation, it stacked one multi-agent orchestrator on top of another, paying double system-prompt overhead (142 s median latency on a 3-file refactor). By contrast, OmO injects in-stream TTSR (<system-interrupt>) nudges that redirect a stuck model without killing its session.

How OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Antigravity solve these problems in-kernel

Auditing m9g-agent-corps against OmO (Oh-My-OpenAgent), OpenCode, Claude Code, and Google Antigravity (agy) clarifies why mature harnesses invest so heavily in their inner execution kernels rather than outer multi-agent wrappers:

Figure 2A. End-to-End Harness Reliability and Inner-Loop Coupling Score (10-Pillar Audit) Composite Score / 10.0 • M9G-TR-2026-02
m9g-agent-corps Standalone CLI (Unwired hooks + regex handoff + 12k middle-slice) 5.8 / 10 (High unit-test coverage, brittle live loop)
Google Antigravity (agy: Sandboxed Linux Worker Container & Skill/IDE Harness) 8.2 / 10 (Strong domain skills & container sandbox)
OpenCode (Go/TS Client-Server Bus + Native LSP Diagnostics + SQLite Session Snapshots) 8.8 / 10 (Clean provider-agnostic TUI + LSP feedback)
Claude Code (Tight Single-Loop Kernel + Exact String Edit Verification + CoW Worktrees) 9.2 / 10 (Minimal delegation tax, high context fidelity)
OmO (Oh-My-OpenAgent) + m9g-mcp Power Tools (Persistent Eval Kernel + Live PTY + TTSR) 9.6 / 10 (Programmatic eval batching + live subagent steering)
Figure 2B. Median 3-File Refactor Latency and Context Fidelity Across Harnesses Wall-Clock Seconds (Lower is Better)
m9g-agent-corps Wrapping Full CLI Subagents (Nested Orchestrator + 300s Blocking Pipe) 142 s • Double summarization loss
m9g-agent-corps Standalone (Rule 1 Mandatory Delegation to Cold-Start Worker + Regex Report) 78 s • 300-word Markdown bottleneck
OpenCode / Antigravity (Direct In-Loop Tool Calls + Per-File Edit & Test Cycle) 34 s • Full in-session context preserved
OmO / Claude Code (Parallel In-Process Read/Edit Batching + Enforced LSP/Test Gate) 24 s (-69% vs. m9g) • 100% typed state survival
M9G Cross-Harness Architectural Comparison • Ref: M9G-TR-2026-02 Author: Minsu Chang, Ph.D. (M9G)
Architectural Dimension m9g-agent-corps (Standalone v0.3) OmO (Oh-My-OpenAgent) OpenCode Claude Code Google Antigravity (agy)
Primary Execution Kernel Python wrapper over google.antigravity.Agent + blocking CLI subprocesses Persistent JS (Bun) & Python eval kernels + PTY session manager Go/TypeScript client-server event bus + provider-agnostic tool loop Tight single-process Node/TS agent loop with native shell & file tools Remote Linux container (Interactions API) + Local IDE/Manager harness
File Read & Context Windowing 12k middle-out slice (4k head + 8k tail deletes lines 120 to 380); built AST skeletonizer Line-indexed offset/limit + parallel batch reads inside eval Line-paginated file reads + automatic LSP symbol & diagnostic context Line-numbered offset/limit reads + structural AST/ripgrep search Windowed file view + container filesystem tools + inline skill context
Code Mutation & Edit Safety Built SHA-256 HashlineEditor (±25-line drift), but unwired in default worker loop Exact disjoint multi-hunk edit + immediate lsp_diagnostics gate Exact string replacement / patch application with automatic LSP check Exact uniqueness-checked string replacement after mandatory file read Container/workspace file mutation + test runner execution
Subagent Delegation & Handoffs Rule 1 mandatory delegation; regex on trailing prose (defaults missing status to SUCCESS) Typed async task / workpool + CoW worktree isolation + task_output peek Scoped child session tasks sharing the local server event bus Targeted Task subagents for parallel exploration; direct main-loop edits Dynamic subagents in Manager mode, or stateless leaf worker via agy -p
Long-Running Process & Terminal Control Blocking 300s subprocess.run (capture_output=True); no mid-turn steering Live PTY sessions (bash_output, bash_input, monitor event wakes) Streaming command runner with user interrupt & output tailing Background bash jobs with live stdout/stderr polling Sandboxed Linux container shell or local auto-mode command runner
Loop Recovery & Verification Gate Hard break kills worker on 3 repeats; verification gates built in sidecar but unwired In-stream TTSR self-healing + enforced V1/V2/V3 diagnostic/test gates LSP error injection into tool result + interactive turn rollback In-loop tool-error feedback + pre-commit hook & test verification Built-in policy hooks + container test verification

Why extracting seven stateless tools into m9g-mcp worked

The post-mortem left one clear conclusion: building a competing outer agent loop wastes effort when OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Antigravity already run tight in-process tool loops, live PTY terminals, and typed error recovery. At the same time, seven stateless modules from src/ag_harness/ solved concrete gaps that those harnesses still encounter on large repositories: 75% to 90% AST token compression, shadow Git index checkpoints that leave staged files untouched, and SHA-256 line-hash batch edits.

In commit cfa9395 (ag_harness/agy_mcp_server.py, 662 lines), we retired the outer orchestrator and shipped those modules as m9g-mcp (m9g-power-tools), a stateless JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio MCP server installed via m9g --install-agy-mcp -w .. Because each tool takes explicit inputs and returns a deterministic JSON payload inside the host harness's own validated tool loop, OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Antigravity gain all seven capabilities with zero extra delegation hops:

  1. m9g_skeletonize (context_controller.py): Parses Python ASTs into function signatures and docstrings, cutting file read tokens by 75% to 90% before full-span inspection.
  2. m9g_checkpoint (checkpoint.py): Creates, diffs, and restores workspace snapshots (create, list, diff, undo, rollback) through a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE (git write-tree and git read-tree) without modifying the user's staged .git/index.
  3. m9g_hashline_read (hashline_tools.py): Reads explicit line ranges with 4-character SHA-256 content hashes (L{n}:{hash}|) and loads subdirectory AGENTS.md rules once per session.
  4. m9g_hashline_edit (hashline_tools.py): Applies bottom-up, hash-verified multi-file edits with ±25-line drift relocation and sub-millisecond Python compile() syntax checks.
  5. m9g_code_intel (hashline_tools.py): Runs structural symbol search (ast_grep), definition lookup, reference lookup, document symbol listing, and docstring hover across Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, and Go.
  6. m9g_memory (memory_store.py): Stores and updates YAML-frontmatter Markdown memory blocks (decisions, architecture, learnings) with automatic wikilink updates.
  7. m9g_gemini_media (gemini_api_cli_bridge.py): Generates speech, images, and video clips (tts, image, video) directly to output_path on disk so binary base64 blobs never enter the model context window.
Research Provenance, Prior Art Disclosure & Anti-Scraping Notice

This technical report (M9G-TR-2026-02), the 28-module m9g-agent-corps codebase (src/ag_harness/), the six-flaw inner-loop post-mortem, the five-harness comparative audit (m9g-agent-corps vs. OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Antigravity), and the seven-tool m9g-mcp server design constitute original published prior art by Minsu Chang, Ph.D. (장민수 / M9G) on mincasurong.github.io. Copying, paraphrasing, or repackaging this systems analysis or telemetry into third-party conference papers or arXiv preprints is prohibited.

ko.articleLede: 우리는 src/ag_harness/에 28개 파이썬 모듈과 169개 통과 단위 테스트를 갖춘 독자 코딩 하네스 m9g-agent-corps를 직접 구현했습니다. 그러나 실제 다중 파일 개발에서는 Oh-My-OpenAgent(OmO), OpenCode, Claude Code, Google Antigravity보다 느리고 취약했습니다. 미연결 편집 훅, 정규식 상태 파싱, 300초 버퍼링 서브프로세스 등 6가지 내부 커널 결함이 원인이었으며, 우리는 외부 루프를 폐기하고 7개 무상태 도구를 m9g-mcp 서버로 분리했습니다.
ko.takeawaysHeader: TL;DR: 실패 복기(Post-Mortem) 요약 및 아키텍처 전환
ko.takeaway1: src/ag_harness/의 28개 모듈과 169개 단위 테스트. 95% 암묵적 캐시 적중($0.10/1M vs. $2.00/1M)을 위한 ImmutablePrefixBuilder, 4자 SHA-256 라인 해시 기반 HashlineEditor 및 75~90% AST 토큰 압축기 skeletonize_python_code(), 임시 GIT_INDEX_FILE 섀도우 체크포인트와 SQLite WAL 저널, FiveTierHookPipeline과 IntentGate, 위상 정렬 DAGEngine, WSL2 브리지 및 GF(2^8) 터미널 QR 리모트까지 6대 핵심 모듈을 구현했습니다.
ko.takeaway2: 실전 신뢰성을 무너뜨린 6가지 내부 커널 결함. argon_omo_substrate.py가 main.py 및 agy_workers.py의 실제 실행 경로와 연결되지 않았고, parse_from_markdown() 정규식 파서는 잘린 응답을 SUCCESS로 오판했으며, 300초 블로킹 subprocess.run 블랙박스, Rule 1 강제 위임과 19개 도구 프롬프트 비대화(78~142초 지연), 120~380행을 잘라내는 중간 삭제 슬라이싱, 3회 반복 시 강제 종료가 결합되어 실전 루프가 흔들렸습니다.
ko.takeaway3: 7개 무상태 도구의 m9g-mcp 서버 추출. OmO의 상주형 Bun/Python eval 커널, OpenCode의 Go/TS 이벤트 버스와 LSP, Claude Code의 단일 프로세스 정밀 편집 루프, Antigravity의 컨테이너 런타임과 외곽 루프로 경쟁하는 대신 7개 무상태 도구를 JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio 기반 m9g-mcp 서버로 분리해 기존 하네스 내부에 장착했습니다.

ja.articleTag: M9G-TR-2026-02 • エージェントシステム & ハーネス工学
ja.articleTitle: マルチエージェント・コーディングハーネスの自作と失敗の記録: m9g-agent-corps vs. OmO、OpenCode、Claude Code、Antigravity
ja.articleLede: 我々はsrc/ag_harness/に28個のPythonモジュールと169件の単体テストを備えた独自コーディングハーネスm9g-agent-corpsを構築しました。しかし日常の複数ファイル改修では、Oh-My-OpenAgent (OmO)、OpenCode、Claude Code、Google Antigravityに速度と信頼性で敗れました。未接続の編集フック、正規表現によるステータス判定、300秒バッファリング子プロセスなど6つの内部カーネル欠陥が原因であり、外部ループを廃止して7つのステートレスツールをm9g-mcpへ抽出しました。
ja.takeawaysHeader: TL;DR: ポストモーテム要約とアーキテクチャ転換
ja.takeaway1: src/ag_harness/の28モジュールと169件の単体テスト。95%暗黙キャッシュ維持 ($0.10/1M vs. $2.00/1M) のImmutablePrefixBuilder、4文字SHA-256行ハッシュ編集器HashlineEditorと75〜90% AST圧縮skeletonize_python_code()、一時GIT_INDEX_FILEシャドウチェックポイントとSQLite WAL履歴、FiveTierHookPipelineとIntentGate、トポロジカルDAGEngine、WSL2ブリッジとGF(2^8) QRリモートを実装しました。
ja.takeaway2: 実運用を破綻させた6つの内部カーネル欠陥。argon_omo_substrate.pyがmain.pyとagy_workers.pyの本番ループに未接続だったこと、parse_from_markdown()が途中切断された応答をSUCCESSと誤判定したこと、300秒同期subprocess.runブラックボックス、Rule 1強制委譲と19ツール束縛による78〜142秒の遅延、cap_tool_output()による120〜380行目の中抜き削除、3回重複での強制breakが重なりました。
ja.takeaway3: 7つのステートレスツールをm9g-mcpへ抽出。OmOの常駐Bun/Python evalカーネル、OpenCodeのGo/TSイベントバスとLSP、Claude Codeの単一プロセス厳密編集ループ、Antigravityのコンテナ実行基盤と競合する外側ループを捨て、JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio対応のm9g-mcpサーバーとして各ハーネス内部へ提供しました。

zh.articleTag: M9G-TR-2026-02 • 智能体系统与编码框架工程
zh.articleTitle: 从零构建多智能体编码框架及其失败复盘: m9g-agent-corps 对比 OmO、OpenCode、Claude Code 与 Antigravity
zh.articleLede: 我们在 src/ag_harness/ 中构建了包含 28 个 Python 模块与 169 项通过单元测试的独立编码框架 m9g-agent-corps。但在日常多文件开发中，其速度与可靠性均落后于 Oh-My-OpenAgent (OmO)、OpenCode、Claude Code 与 Google Antigravity。未挂载编辑钩子、正则状态误判与 300 秒缓冲子进程等六项内核缺陷导致了失败；我们最终废弃外层编排器，将七项无状态工具提取为 m9g-mcp。
zh.takeawaysHeader: TL;DR: 失败复盘摘要与架构转型
zh.takeaway1: src/ag_harness/ 中的 28 个模块与 169 项通过测试。我们实现了六大核心模块: 保障 95% 隐式缓存命中的 ImmutablePrefixBuilder ($0.10/1M 对比 $2.00/1M)、4 字符 SHA-256 哈希行编辑器 HashlineEditor 与压缩率达 75% 至 90% 的 skeletonize_python_code()、基于临时 GIT_INDEX_FILE 的影子 Git 检查点与 SQLite WAL 日志、FiveTierHookPipeline 与 IntentGate、拓扑波次调度 DAGEngine，以及 WSL2 桥接与 GF(2^8) 终端二维码远程控制。
zh.takeaway2: 六项内环内核缺陷击穿日常可靠性。单元测试通过并未挽救真实运行环路: argon_omo_substrate.py 未接入 main.py 与 agy_workers.py；parse_from_markdown() 将截断输出默认误判为 SUCCESS；spawn_agy_worker() 用 300 秒缓冲 subprocess.run 黑盒阻塞子智能体；Rule 1 强制委派与 19 个工具定义使 1 至 3 文件修改耗时增至 78 至 142 秒；cap_tool_output() 掐头去尾删掉了第 120 至 380 行代码；StreamLoopMonitor 在三次重复调用时直接硬中断会话。
zh.takeaway3: 提取七项无状态工具至 m9g-mcp 取得实效。我们不再维护与 OmO 常驻 Bun/Python eval 内核、OpenCode Go/TS 事件总线与 LSP、Claude Code 单进程精确编辑环路以及 Antigravity 容器运行时竞争的外层循环，而是将七项无状态工具封装为 JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio MCP 服务 (m9g-power-tools) 供成熟框架直接调用。

es.articleTag: M9G-TR-2026-02 • Sistemas Agénticos e Ingeniería de Harnesses
es.articleTitle: Construyendo un Harness de Codificación Multi-Agente desde Cero y Por Qué Fracasó: m9g-agent-corps frente a OmO, OpenCode, Claude Code y Antigravity
es.articleLede: Construimos m9g-agent-corps, un harness de codificación en Python con 28 módulos en src/ag_harness/ y 169 pruebas unitarias superadas. En tareas diarias multi-archivo perdió en velocidad y fiabilidad frente a Oh-My-OpenAgent, OpenCode, Claude Code y Google Antigravity. Seis fallos del bucle interno causaron ese resultado, incluidos hooks desconectados, parseo regex y subprocesos bloqueantes de 300 segundos. Retiramos el orquestador externo y extrajimos siete herramientas sin estado en m9g-mcp.
es.takeawaysHeader: TL;DR: Resumen Post-Mortem y Pivote Arquitectónico
es.takeaway1: 28 módulos y 169 pruebas unitarias en src/ag_harness/. Construimos seis módulos centrales: ImmutablePrefixBuilder para retener el 95% de caché implícita en Gemini ($0.10/1M vs. $2.00/1M), HashlineEditor (hashes SHA-256 de 4 caracteres, reubicación de +-25 líneas y chequeo AST en menos de 1 ms) junto con skeletonize_python_code() (75% a 90% menos tokens), puntos de control Git con GIT_INDEX_FILE temporal y SQLite WAL, FiveTierHookPipeline con IntentGate, DAGEngine topológico y puente WSL2 con control QR GF(2^8).
es.takeaway2: Seis fallos del kernel interno rompieron la fiabilidad diaria. argon_omo_substrate.py quedó desconectado de main.py y agy_workers.py; WorkerHandoffReport.parse_from_markdown() marcó como SUCCESS respuestas truncadas; spawn_agy_worker() encerró subagentes CLI en subprocess.run bloqueantes de 300 s; la delegación obligatoria de la Regla 1 y 19 herramientas elevaron la latencia a 78-142 s; cap_tool_output() borró las líneas 120 a 380; y StreamLoopMonitor abortó turnos al tercer intento repetido.
es.takeaway3: Extraer siete herramientas sin estado en m9g-mcp funcionó. En lugar de mantener un bucle externo frente a los kernels persistentes Bun/Python de OmO, el bus Go/TS con LSP de OpenCode, el bucle único de edición exacta de Claude Code y el contenedor de Antigravity, empaquetamos siete herramientas deterministas en un servidor MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 por stdio (m9g-power-tools).
